findings.title: Migration crashes when no category matches the old embed setting
findings.body: The query joining `site_settings.value` to `categories.name` commonly returns no rows when the old `embed_category` setting is blank (its default) or references a deleted category. Indexing `[0]['id']` then dereferences nil before the intended `category_id == 0` fallback can run, causing the migration to abort and preventing upgrades. Handle an empty result before accessing its first row and then fall back to the uncategorized category.

findings.title: Duplicate host mappings can select an arbitrary category
findings.body: There is no uniqueness validation or database unique index for `host`, while `record_for_host` uses `.first`. An admin can create multiple rows for the same hostname with different category IDs; subsequent imports will use whichever row the database happens to return first, so embedded topics can be filed into an unintended category. Enforce a case-insensitive unique host mapping (including a unique database index) or define deterministic conflict behavior.

findings.title: Hosts configured with a port can never be matched
findings.body: The validation explicitly permits values such as `example.com:8080`, and the normalization callback preserves the port, but `record_for_host` parses an incoming URL and compares only `uri.host`, which is `example.com` and never includes `:8080`. Such an allowed host saves successfully but all embed requests from it are rejected and imports receive no category. Either normalize stored hosts to hostname-only and disallow ports, or compare an appropriate host-and-port value consistently.

findings.title: Updating a nonexistent host raises a server error
findings.body: `EmbeddableHost.where(...).first` returns nil for an unknown ID and is passed to `save_host`, which immediately calls `host.host=`. This produces a 500 instead of a not-found response for stale or invalid admin requests. The destroy action has the same nil dereference at line 16. Fetch with a not-found-aware lookup or explicitly return 404 before updating/destroying.
